stemBlocks.value: A rescue boat travels 15 km due east from harbour H to Q, then 8 km due north to R. a) Calculate the direct distance HR. b) The harbour radio has a range of 16 km. Determine whether the boat at R is within range, showing the comparison used. c) Calculate how much shorter the direct journey HR is than the two-stage journey HQR.
Think first: East and north are perpendicular, so the two legs of the journey are the legs of a right-angled triangle.

solutionSteps.instruction: Note the right angle at Q.

contentBlocks.value: Due east and due north are perpendicular directions
Result: the boat is out of range
Result: the direct route is 6 km shorter

strategyBlocks.value: Use Pythagoras on the 15 km and 8 km legs to get HR, compare it with the 16 km range, then subtract HR from the total travelled.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) HR = 17 km  (b) No — HR = 17 km which is greater than the 16 km range, so the boat at R is outside radio range  (c) the direct journey is 6 km shorter (23 km − 17 km)

whyThisWorks.value: Compass directions that differ by 90° always produce a right-angled triangle, so Pythagoras converts two perpendicular legs into a single straight-line distance. Part c makes the triangle inequality concrete: any two sides of a triangle together exceed the third, which is exactly why going direct always beats going round two sides.
